description: Every update from every ecosystem lands in one weekly PR: crates, the Rust toolchain, GitHub Actions, and every pin in the Python lock file, transitive ones included, since a pip freeze lists them all.

Cargo's transitive dependencies are the one thing that cannot join it: Renovate refuses to group a lock file refresh with other update types, so `cargo update` arrives as a second PR the same morning.

A release has to be three days old before it is offered, which is the cheapest defence there is against a package taken over the day it is published. Vulnerability fixes skip the wait and the schedule.

packageRules.description: The manifests name the versions the binary is built with, so an in-range update moves the manifest as well as the lock rather than leaving the two to drift apart.

pip_requirements.description: requirements.txt holds loose floors on purpose and is left alone; requirements.lock is the pip freeze a run was actually made with, and every pin in it is kept current.
